title: Arjuna at the northern gate
hookLine: the four brothers ride to the four directions; at the edge of the world, Arjuna keeps a sacred limit
carry: maryada: some ground you don't take

lines: A PLACE WITH NOTHING TO WIN.
cards: Back at Indraprastha, the plan gets bigger. If kings are going to honor Yudhishthira, the brothers will have to go and meet them first. So the younger four divide the world.
Arjuna rides north. Bhima rides east. Sahadeva rides south.
Nakula rides west. Yudhishthira stays home in the hall, with Dhaumya and his friends around him. Each brother will come back with the tribute of kings.
And one will come back from a place where there was nothing to win.

teach.b: The text follows each brother in turn: kingdoms, battles, and kings who submit or welcome them and send gifts. But one moment at the northern edge stands apart.
Arjuna rides on, past mountain after mountain, to the land of the Northern Kurus. At the gate, powerful guards stop him, and they speak kindly. You can't conquer this place, they say.
Even if you came in, you couldn't see anything with human eyes. We're pleased with you. Tell us what you want.
And Arjuna doesn't push. I want my brother to be sovereign, he says. If this land is closed to humans, I won't enter.
Give something as tribute, and I'll go.
They give him fine cloth, ornaments and skins, and he turns back. The greatest archer of his age, who won Draupadi with his bow, meets a boundary and keeps it.
Hindus have a word for that: maryada, the right limit, the line you don't cross even when you could. It's why Rama is called maryada purushottama, the best of men, who kept the bounds.
And it's built into ordinary worship.

teach.h: SHOES OFF AT THE TEMPLE DOOR.
teach.b: Shoes come off at the temple door. Many people touch the step before they go in.
And the inner shrine, the garbhagriha, where the murti sits, is in many temples for the priests alone; everyone else takes darshan from just outside.
Holy ground is entered asking, not taking. This week ran from a father's message to a prison opened and four brothers coming home with the world's gifts. Tomorrow, the Rajasuya itself.

how: The word digvijaya, conquest of the directions, outlived the epic: tradition uses it for the travels of the teacher Shankara, whose victories are told as debates won across India rather than battles.

o: the royal rite the brothers ride out to win tribute for
a gift of cloth and skins from the Northern Kurus
a march to conquer every land in all four directions

games.q: the four directions, and the kept limit — tap the pairs.
p: the limit you keep even when you could cross
the inner shrine, in many temples for priests

s: Arjuna forced his way into the land of the Northern Kurus
the guards said nothing there could be conquered, and he asked only for tribute.
Hindu worshippers may walk anywhere in a temple
many temples keep the garbhagriha for the priests; worshippers take darshan from just outside.
the Northern Kurus sent Arjuna away with gifts
fine cloth, ornaments and skins, as tribute for Yudhishthira.

games.q: you're Arjuna at the edge of the world. kind guards say you can't conquer this land and couldn't see it with human eyes anyway. what do you do?
o: fight your way through the gate.
ask for tribute for your brother and turn back.
games.why: he won't enter a land closed to humans and asks for tribute instead. that's maryada, the kept limit, the same virtue that makes Rama maryada purushottama.

practice: Find the nearest doorway, or picture the door of a temple or a place that's holy to you. Many Hindus touch the temple step, then their forehead, before they go in.
If you pray, do that, or simply bow your head at the threshold and step through asking, not taking. If you don't, stop at the doorway for one slow breath and notice the line you're crossing.

wordCard.voice: The Rajasuya. Today the brothers ride to the four directions to win kings' tribute for it, and at the northern edge Arjuna keeps a limit.

orig.note: Sanskrit digvijaya: 'victory over the directions', the name of the section in which the brothers ride out.

carryVoice: Your line: maryada, some ground you don't take. The greatest archer stopped at a gate and asked. See you at the Rajasuya.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Digvijaya Parva (the four brothers ride to the four directions; Arjuna at the land of the Northern Kurus)
